pharm: Inhibits sodium-chloride reabsorption in the distal convoluted tubule, increasing excretion of sodium, chloride and water, lowering plasma volume and blood pressure.
quick: Hypertension 12.5-50 mg once daily; edema 25-100 mg/day
Take with or without food; take in the morning to limit nighttime urination
Generally avoided; may cause fetal/neonatal jaundice, thrombocytopenia, electrolyte disturbance
Excreted in milk; high doses may suppress lactation
Largely ineffective if CrCl <30 mL/min; use loop diuretic instead
Use caution; fluid/electrolyte shifts may precipitate hepatic encephalopathy
Electrolytes (K, Na, Ca, Mg), renal function, glucose, uric acid, blood pressure
summary: Hydrochlorothiazide is a thiazide diuretic used to treat hypertension and edema from heart failure, hepatic cirrhosis, renal disease, and corticosteroid/estrogen therapy. It acts on the distal tubule to promote sodium and water excretion. Common metabolic effects include hypokalemia, hyponatremia, hyperuricemia, hyperglycemia and hypercalcemia; it is a sulfonamide-derived drug and loses efficacy in significant renal impairment.
indications: Hypertension, alone or combined with other antihypertensives
Edema associated with congestive heart failure, hepatic cirrhosis, and renal dysfunction
Edema due to corticosteroid or estrogen therapy

dosage.d: 12.5-25 mg once daily; may increase to 50 mg/day
dosage.n: Doses above 25 mg add little BP effect but increase metabolic risk

dosage.d: 25-100 mg once or twice daily; intermittent dosing (alternate days) may suffice
dosage.n: Titrate to response; lowest effective dose

dosage.d: ~1-2 mg/kg/day in 1-2 divided doses; infants <6 mo up to 3 mg/kg/day
dosage.n: Use weight-based dosing; max generally 50 mg/day in children
Consider a loop diuretic if GFR is low

admin: Administer in the morning to reduce nocturnal diuresis
Establish a baseline and monitor serum electrolytes periodically
Encourage adequate but not excessive potassium intake; potassium supplement or sparing agent if hypokalemia develops
moa: Hydrochlorothiazide inhibits the sodium-chloride cotransporter (NCC) in the distal convoluted tubule, blocking reabsorption of sodium and chloride. The resulting natriuresis and diuresis reduce extracellular fluid volume and, with chronic use, lower peripheral vascular resistance, decreasing blood pressure. Increased delivery of sodium to the distal nephron enhances potassium and hydrogen secretion (hypokalemia, metabolic alkalosis), while calcium reabsorption is increased.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to hydrochlorothiazide or other sulfonamide-derived drugs
relative: Severe hepatic impairment / risk of hepatic coma

preg: Thiazides cross the placenta; use in pregnancy may cause fetal or neonatal jaundice, thrombocytopenia, and electrolyte disturbances and does not prevent or treat pre-eclampsia. Generally avoided unless clearly necessary.
lact: Hydrochlorothiazide is excreted in breast milk; high doses may suppress lactation. Use with caution and monitor the infant.
renal: Efficacy declines and the drug may be ineffective when creatinine clearance falls below ~30 mL/min; azotemia may worsen. A loop diuretic is preferred in significant renal impairment.
hepatic: Use with caution in hepatic impairment or progressive liver disease; minor fluid and electrolyte shifts may precipitate hepatic coma.

major: Lithium (thiazides reduce renal lithium clearance, risk of lithium toxicity)
Drugs that prolong QT or cause torsades when hypokalemia present (e.g., sotalol, dofetilide)
moderate: NSAIDs (reduce diuretic/antihypertensive effect, risk of renal impairment)
Antidiabetic drugs (hyperglycemia may require dose adjustment)
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; maintain consistent dietary sodium/potassium.
interactions.diagnostics: May raise serum calcium, glucose, uric acid, and cholesterol; can interfere with parathyroid function tests.

serious: Acute angle-closure glaucoma / acute myopia (idiosyncratic, early)
Non-melanoma skin cancer with long-term use
rare: Acute respiratory distress / non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema
emergency: Severe hyponatremia/hypokalemia with arrhythmia or seizures
Acute angle-closure glaucoma (sudden eye pain, vision loss)

monitoring: Serum electrolytes (K, Na, Mg, Ca) periodically
Blood glucose and serum uric acid
Blood pressure and signs of volume depletion
Skin examination for non-melanoma skin cancer with prolonged use
counsel: Take in the morning to avoid waking at night to urinate
Report muscle cramps, weakness, severe dizziness, or palpitations (possible low potassium)
Use sunscreen and protective clothing; report new or changing skin lesions
Rise slowly to avoid dizziness; report sudden eye pain or vision changes
Maintain adequate fluid and a potassium-rich diet unless told otherwise
pk: Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); protect from light and moisture
pearls: Unlike loop diuretics, thiazides decrease urinary calcium - useful in calcium kidney stones and osteoporosis
Loses effectiveness when GFR <30 mL/min; switch to a loop diuretic
Monitor for hyponatremia, especially in elderly women on low-sodium intake
Low doses (12.5-25 mg) give most of the antihypertensive benefit with less metabolic toxicity
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered; if it is late in the day or almost time for the next dose, skip it to avoid nighttime urination. Do not double the dose.
overdose: Overdose causes excessive diuresis with dehydration, electrolyte depletion (hypokalemia, hyponatremia, hypochloremia), hypotension, weakness, and possible cardiac arrhythmias. Management is supportive: replace fluids and electrolytes, monitor cardiac and renal function; there is no specific antidote and the drug is not efficiently removed by hemodialysis.
